purpose: Defines the logical data model of doc-link: information entities, identifiers, sources, relationships, multiplicity, and value meaning and freshness, without specifying a physical schema.
summary: Model boundary: current artifacts and the last committed index are separate; no notification state is held
Table of logical entities: document identity, target spec, observation, document info, reference description, check result, section entry, final check state, committed ToC, build run
Document info is stored once per document ID and shared by all keys, never copied per key
Committed ToC holds membership, references, reflected hashes, and check results, not document info
Multiplicity: documents may belong to multiple keys and have multiple references; at most one committed ToC per key
Reverse references are derived only from scanned referrers, not all referrers in the world
Sections are identified by heading-end section IDs; sections without a DLID have no stable identity
Document ID and content hash differ; link path fixes change the content hash
Reference check match holds only for the recorded directory and check time
Documents leaving the index target are removed from the committed ToC; no unresolved relations remain
tasks: Designing or revising the doc-link data model
Implementing storage of document info and committed ToC
Implementing reference description and check result handling
Handling section entries and section IDs
Reasoning about freshness of ToC versus current files
Reviewing multi-key behavior of the same document ID
